summary: Forensic sampling and immutable playback export for AML due-diligence
description:
Issue summary: NorthLake Financial (enterprise) requests a timebound, forensic-grade slice of their audit activity for M&A due-diligence. The deliverable must be cryptographically verifiable and include a chain-of-custody manifest, per-record SHA256 checksums, resume tokens, and an immutable playback harness.

Impact: Customer needs the export to complete before legal review next week. Failure to provide verifiable artifacts delays M&A closing and may escalate to legal.

Environment: Production tenant for NorthLake, us-east-1, activity window requested: 2026-02-15T00:00:00Z through 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z.

Request / Deliverables:
- NDJSON export of audit events for the window, tenant-scoped.
- Per-record SHA256 and a top-level manifest listing batch checksums and resume tokens.
- RFC3161 timestamping of the manifest (or documented alternative if not available).
- Proof that exported objects were taken from append-only archive (S3 Object Lock) & KMS key id used.
- Playable replay harness (small Docker container) that can stream events in chronological order to a provided consumer endpoint, including resume semantics.
- Short runbook that documents verification steps for an auditor.

Requested delivery date: 2026-03-13 (customer gave written deadline).
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - export/forensic request. Customer provided sample event IDs and timeframe: event_ids: [evt-48391, evt-48392, evt-49104]. Customer asked to verify those IDs are present in the slice and to provide per-event checksums.

investigation_notes:
2026-03-09: Triage call with CS, SRE, and CustOps. Confirmed tenant object-lock was enabled during window.
2026-03-10: SRE verified S3 retention metadata for the tenant and located three archival partitions covering the requested window.
Hypotheses: 1) Export is straightforward using existing archive extractor but needs deterministic chunk ordering. 2) RFC3161 stamping must be proxied via our CA partner; if delayed, provide manifest with KMS-signed HMAC as interim.
Findings: The archive contains duplicated delivery receipts for high-volume partitions; dedupe required by event_id canonicalization.
Constraints: Large export (~12GB) — need to run on dedicated job runner (reserved capacity) to meet SLA.

resolution_notes:
Status as of 2026-03-12: Export job completed to staging S3 path s3://redwood-exports/northlake/SUP-791413/2026-02-15_2026-02-28/; produced: 1) northlake_slice.ndjson.gz (12.3GB), 2) manifest.json.sha256 (top-level batch checksum), 3) per_record_sha256.csv, 4) resume_tokens.txt, 5) docker-replay-harness.tar.gz.
Delivered to customer presigned-download and via secure SFTP (per contract) at 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC.
RFC3161: vendor stamped manifest received 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC and uploaded to the export path.
Chain-of-custody: S3 object-lock metadata and KMS key arn included in exported manifest.
Workaround/fix: N/A (request fulfilled).
Follow-up items: 1) Create a small playbook in Confluence describing verification steps for auditors (owner: CustOps), 2) Add deterministic dedupe to archive extractor for future requests (owner: infra-team, linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-tooling/pull/412).

- Consider exposing a self-serve 'forensic export' flow in Console for enterprise customers (product discovery ticket recommended).
